$comment: C 6.4.4.4p7 (D-CSUBSET-NARROW-HEX-ESCAPE-TRUNCATED-TO-TWO-DIGITS) fail-loud witness: in "a\xFFb" the trailing `b` IS a hex digit, so the escape is \xFFb = 0xFFB and it overflows a one-byte element. DSS used to emit `61 FF 62 00` here - matching NO reference in either direction. MEASURED 2026-09-02, each compiled and RUN: gcc 13.3.0 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 accept by TRUNCATING to `61 FB 00` with a warning, clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51 REFUSE. A reference that only accepts by narrowing the value away is not one that WORKS, so the union over what works is a refusal. The load-bearing pin is the CODE plus a rejected compile at the literal position; the message names the WIDTH and the VALUE because neither alone is actionable.
